headline: TECHNICAL LEAD
& SOFTWARE ARCHITECT
hero.subheadline: Architecture that teams can actually move on.

about.title: The person behind the architecture
paragraphs: I am a software architect and technical lead from Plovdiv, Bulgaria, with over a decade of experience building and modernizing systems for clients ranging from five-person startups to global financial institutions. Most of my career has revolved around Java and the Spring ecosystem, but what defines my work is not a framework — it is the ability to take a system everyone is afraid to touch and turn it into something teams can move fast on.

I gravitate toward the hardest version of every problem: legacy platforms with decades of accumulated decisions, clients whose trust has been burned by failed attempts, and programs where the roadmap itself needs to be reinvented. That is where architecture stops being diagrams and becomes leadership.

My background in competitive sports — football and wrestling — shaped how I operate professionally: disciplined preparation, calm under pressure, and an instinct for making a team greater than the sum of its parts.

stats.label: Clients — from startups to global enterprises

flagship.title: Modernizing a 35-year-old core banking platform
flagship.summary: A complete migration of one of the financial industry's most entrenched systems — a commercial lending platform with over 35 years of accumulated code — to a modern technology stack. Several companies had attempted it before and failed. This is the story of how the program was turned around.

challenge.title: The challenge
challenge.text: The client arrived guarded and skeptical — previous vendors had promised the same migration and failed to deliver, and our continued engagement was far from guaranteed. The codebase carried more than three decades of business-critical logic that no single person fully understood. A conventional rewrite plan was never going to survive contact with reality, and the client knew it.

approach.title: How I turned it around
bullets: During discovery, I stood out as a key figure by building proof-of-concept AI automation tools that demonstrated — not promised — that the migration was achievable. Those POCs visibly shifted the client's attitude from skepticism to confidence.

I designed a new target architecture and an AI-driven automation roadmap that completely reshaped the program's original plan. That roadmap was adopted and made me the Project Technical Lead and Main Architect.
I architected the suite of migration automation tooling that is in place today, systematically converting the legacy codebase instead of relying on error-prone manual rewrites.

I defined how the program itself runs: pod structures, the way teams interact, client communication, planning, and milestone acceptance — from interviewing and staffing in the early days to steering every technical decision now.

impact.title: Where it stands
bullets: The program is executing on my architecture and roadmap, with a team of more than 60 engineers working toward the complete migration of the platform.
I am the central point of technical direction — implementation questions, architectural decisions, and cross-team alignment all flow through me.
A client that once doubted the engagement would continue now treats the program as its path forward — trust rebuilt through working software, not slideware.

The AI automation approach avoids the pitfalls that sank previous attempts: instead of an army of developers manually re-reading 35 years of code, tooling does the heavy lifting while engineers verify, harden, and extend.

timelineSection.title: From first commit to program architect

Direct technical decision-making across all pods; define team topology, planning, and milestone acceptance with the client.
Serve as the single point of alignment — engineers, leads, and client stakeholders route implementation and architecture questions through me.

timeline.summary: Architect within a team of 8–10 professionals, working closely with enterprise clients on solution design and delivery.
highlights: Led research and architectural documentation; reviewed code and supported delivery teams.
Collaborated directly with clients and cross-functional teams, delivering technical presentations and guidance.

timeline.summary: Backend development for a telecom (MVNO) platform provider, building and maintaining high-availability Java services.
highlights: Developed and maintained core backend services in a telecom-grade environment.

timeline.summary: A one-man show: analyzed a client's entire business, then designed and built a custom ERP that automated most of their processes and eliminated duplicate data entry.

Order tracking, live stock availability, barcode scanning, complex formula-based pricing, and document/invoice printing.

Taught Spring to students, interviewed candidates, and approved their hiring into the company.
Led a team of trainees and junior developers on client deliveries.
